record.title: A paper reports trace-audited human-agent teams conducting synchrotron X-ray experiments
record.summary: An arXiv preprint submitted on 6 November 2026 at 08:33:55 UTC describes VISION-CC, a team of specialized coding agents grounded in validated scientific tools, conducting three human-guided synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering experiments on nanoparticle superlattices at Brookhaven’s NSLS-II 11-BM beamline. The authors report complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts and an audit pipeline for decision provenance. Their audit estimates that 61–67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while methodological/scientific contributions rose from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56–61% in later experiments. The authors describe the interaction shares as approximate and limit the study to one scientist, beamline and agent platform. The team, audit codebook, a subset of experimental frames and a sanitized ledger excerpt are available; full audit data are available by request.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv record lists v1 of the preprint on auditable human-agent teams for autonomous X-ray experimentation as submitted on 6 November 2026 at 08:33:55 UTC.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that VISION-CC conducted three human-guided transmission small-angle X-ray scattering experiments on nanoparticle superlattices at Brookhaven National Laboratory’s NSLS-II 11-BM CMS beamline, using specialized agent roles and validated scientific software for instrument operation, analysis and adaptive sampling.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that 61–67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, and that methodological/scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56–61% in later experiments. They characterize the message-share estimate as approximate because annotator agreement is limited.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper links a public release of the VISION-CC team, audit codebook, a subset of SAXS frames from Experiment 2 and a sanitized audit-ledger excerpt; it says full audit data are available upon reasonable request subject to facility security policy.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed paper does not establish that the workflow or audit findings generalize beyond one scientist, one beamline and one agent platform, or that the reported results have been independently reproduced.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent group has reproduced the workflow, experiment outcomes or audit statistics in the reviewed evidence.
Evidence comes from one scientist, one beamline and one agent platform; transfer across facilities, teams, tasks or models is unknown.

The authors report weak agreement for the broad message-level interpretation/judgment label, making the 61–67% share approximate; the underlying full transcripts and audit data are not openly available.
No matched measurement of experiment quality, cycle time, engineering labor or total cost against a non-agent workflow was identified.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported workflow and trace-based audit transfer, they could change how physical-science agents are engineered and evaluated; the evidence is a single-scientist, one-beamline case and does not establish generality.
limitations: Single-scientist, one-beamline, one-platform case series; no demonstrated cross-domain generality.
Reported interaction labels have uncertainty; authors call the headline message-share approximate.
No independent reproduction or matched baseline for scientific outcome, cycle time, labor or cost.
Full audit data are request-only; the public release contains selected data and a sanitized ledger excerpt.
brief.summary: An arXiv preprint submitted on 6 November 2026 at 08:33:55 UTC describes VISION-CC, a team of specialized coding agents grounded in validated scientific tools, conducting three human-guided synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering experiments on nanoparticle superlattices at Brookhaven’s NSLS-II 11-BM beamline. The authors report complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts and an audit pipeline for decision provenance. Their audit estimates that 61–67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while methodological/scientific contributions rose from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56–61% in later experiments. The authors describe the interaction shares as approximate and limit the study to one scientist, beamline and agent platform. The team, audit codebook, a subset of experimental frames and a sanitized ledger excerpt are available; full audit data are available by request.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report sustained natural-language-guided physical experiments and aggregate audit statistics for three experiment sessions; these are paper-reported findings, not independently reproduced results.
technical.compute_or_cost: No comparable end-to-end model/API expenditure or cost-per-experiment baseline was identified in the reviewed sections.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected preprint and linked availability statement establish that the authors report these experiments, audit procedures and partial artifacts. The actual experimental runs and audit classifications were not independently verified in this activation.
technical.mechanism: VISION-CC uses Claude Code agent teams with specialized Operator, Analyst, Gaussian-process and reporting roles grounded by domain-specific instructions and validated tools (Bluesky beamline control, SciAnalysis X-ray analysis and gpCAM adaptive sampling). An Audit cog reconstructs proposals, decisions and corrections from retained human-agent and agent-agent transcripts.
technical.regime: Three transmission small-angle X-ray scattering sessions on two nanoparticle-superlattice samples at NSLS-II 11-BM CMS, guided by one scientist and implemented with one agent platform.
technical.reproducibility: The paper links source code, an audit codebook, selected experimental frames and a sanitized audit ledger. Full audit data are request-only subject to facility security policy; no independent build or reproduction was conducted.
technical.strongest_baseline: The study is a descriptive case series; it does not provide a matched non-agent baseline for experiment quality, time, cost or scientific discovery.

brief.title: A paper reports trace-audited human-agent teams conducting synchrotron X-ray experiments
brief.why_it_matters: If trace-audited agent teams can lower the engineering barrier to physical experimentation, they could extend agentic systems from computational workflows into real scientific instruments. This paper offers a concrete but narrow case and a decision-provenance approach; it does not show general scientific autonomy, independent replication or improved experiment economics.
